input.question: What causes lightning
input.ground_truth: Friction of the air and water vapor for the most part. it's a big amospheric version of dragging your socks across the carpet. As air masses grind past one another on their respective paths within the turbulence that is a storm, they exchange electrons, differences accumulate, charges build and eventually lightning occurs. Fun fact: most lightning is cloud to cloud lightning.

Okay! Imagine the sky is like a big blanket, and sometimes it gets really, really bumpy inside it because of warm and cold air mixing up. When the bumpy air gets really, really excited, it makes a big spark—like when you rub a balloon on your hair and then zap your friend!

That big spark is **lightning**! It happens because the air gets so mixed up and charged up that it can’t hold it in anymore, so ZAP! You see a bright flash—that’s lightning! ⚡

So, **lightning is caused by the sky getting all mixed up and making a big spark.**
